paper_title: DeltaEdit Enhancing Sequential Editing in Large Language Models by   Controlling Superimposed Noise
caption: : labelformat=parens, labelsep=period
model_annotation: The line plot, titled "GPT2-XL," illustrates the performance of two editing methods, AlphaEdit and DeltaEdit, measured by two different metrics across a sequence of data points. The plot features an unlabelled linear x-axis with values ranging from approximately 200 to 3000, displaying major tick marks that begin at 500 and are spaced at intervals of 500. There are two linear y-axes: the left y-axis is labeled "Efficacy_{top}" with values ranging from 86 to 100 in increments of 2, while the right y-axis is labeled "noise_E" with values ranging from 2 to 12 in increments of 2. The dashed light red line with square markers represents AlphaEdit Efficacy_{top} mapped to the left y-axis; it begins at approximately 99.5, experiences a gradual decline to roughly 98.8 at x=1000, and then declines more steeply to finish at exactly 86 at x=3000. The dashed light purple line with square markers denotes DeltaEdit Efficacy_{top}, also mapped to the left y-axis, starting near 99.5 at the beginning of the x-axis and demonstrating a steady decline to end at approximately 93.8 at x=3000. The solid light red line with circular markers indicates AlphaEdit noise_E, corresponding to the right y-axis; it starts at approximately 2.8 and exhibits a continuous, upward trend across the entire x-axis, culminating at exactly 12 at x=3000. Finally, the solid light purple line with circular markers represents DeltaEdit noise_E, which maps to the right y-axis, begins at approximately 2.3, rises steadily across the plot, and reaches an ending value of approximately 11.4 at x=3000.
